answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small, time-locked stake before it may sign transactions — a voyage every new identity must pay for. The stake mirrors the agent's claimed reputation: a quill that writes contracts without backing loses its deposit when peers flag fake work. Creating thousands of identities then costs thousands of stakes, while honest agents earn the deposit back with interest. Cheap talk dies; only agents willing to put real value behind their words can trade.
